沙漠地区，稳定50——60分钟之间卡死，唯一一次打了120分钟，结果死亡卡住了，不算成就，后面试了几次，都是卡死到50到六十分钟，无法完成成就。 解决了，我的解决方式是，把除游戏和steam平台以外的所有无关软件全关，且在游戏中，开始游戏时关闭所有声音，窗口化，关闭垂直同步，画质调到最低，进行到四十八分钟左右一直向一个方向奔跑，直至视野中无法出现红色的激光怪，此过程中不再出现卡顿，未响应情况。 虽然可以以此种方式完成成就，但我推测应该是算法无法支持五十分钟到六十分钟怪的数量和各种攻击特效导致游戏崩溃，理由是六十分钟之后直至一百二十分钟期间再未有卡顿现象出现（在第一次卡顿等待几个小时，然后死亡未解锁成就时了解到的情况，希望开发者能继续优化游戏，可以看看沙漠五十到六十分钟算法是否需要调整，因解锁了全成就，特此改为好评，游戏简单易上手，再少些bug就更好了。

[h1][b]小鸡大战青蛙的类幸存者[/b][/h1] 《Machick》是一款动物题材像素风类幸存者游戏。 游戏开始用几张精美的像素插画交代了剧情，邪恶的青蛙部队入侵了鸡的家园，但这些鸡也不是好惹的，其拥有能使用各种魔法的魔杖。 小鸡的这只魔杖还可以自定义，游戏开始前玩家可以选择带有不同攻击方式的魔杖主体、附加攻击特效的木材和核心。 游戏的方式边喝大部分类幸存者一致，敌人会从四面涌来，玩家只需要操控小鸡走位即可。 升级后会出现经典的技能三选一环节，除了增加生命值、移速、拾取范围等基础属性外，还有诸如闪电、火焰、龙卷风、激光之类的魔法。 游戏的场景上还会时不时刷出一些奖励箱子，按照界面上出现的箭头便可找到。 试玩下来，《Machick》的表现中规中矩，除了魔杖自定义外没有特别亮眼的点了，放在如今多如牛毛的类幸存者里显得过于平庸。 [quote]欢迎关注我们的鉴赏家:[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35402982/]走心评测[/url] ←遵从内心，写出真实感受 欢迎加入我们Steam组:[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/ZXPC]走心评测[/url]←点击加入，一起探索游戏的乐趣 喜欢这篇评论，也麻烦点个赞，让更多人能够看到！[/quote]

its fine but there are better games especially for this price. graphics randomly disappearing (including enemies/projectiles that can still kill you!), the UI will disappear randomly during longer runs (15 min+). Poor optimization (GPU: RTX3080TI OC 12GB, CPU: Intel 11th gen i7 11700k overclocked at 2x, both were tanking during final run so I had to set max resource usage at system level) Level ups are the exact same every single run, there's way too little variety and specific weapons are wayyyy stronger than others due to the 'relics' you find during the run favoring specific weapons. Some weapons have 6+ relics, others have literally no relics at all making those weapons completely obsolete. Evolutions have some extremely poor balance, some turning the weapon completely useless compared to the original weapon. My final gripe with this title is the blatant lies on level ups and relics. Some relics don't even work at all if you evolve a weapon and then get the relic afterwards. It can't be a translation issue either because I'm talking about numbers, sure the translations are rough in some places but how the f*ck do you mix up the numbers 8 and 64 in the number of shots?? Looking at you, arcane shots. If you're a true fan of the Vampire survivors genre it's fine for maybe 1,50 or 2 bucks on sale? It felt like a waste of my time though. Fun game, but seemingly abandoned while half-finished. When I bought this game, a news post was made mid-2024 promising new features, but eventually deleted. An update was randomly made after 8 months of no activity that added a new Santa Chicken and Snow Map. The Santa Chicken is bugged and impossible to select. The new map has a bug that makes it impossible to complete. On top of that, the old Desert Map is now locked behind clearing the impossible Snow Map, meaning the game now has one less map than it did before the update. (the Desert Map, when it was working, was also impossible to clear, but the developers promised it was a work in progress that would someday be completed, but never was) The "Play the Game for 1 hour" achievement is also now likely impossible due to the Desert Map being inaccessible. You MIGHT be able to still get it by standing around on the empty Snow map for an hour, though. These bugs have been in the game for months without the developers patching them. EDIT: 5 months after these bugs were added to the game, the developers seemingly got tired of people asking why the winter map was broken. Instead of fixing it, they simply removed it and the Santa chicken from the game entire.

[b]MACHICK[/b], is just a sad game full of empty promises and false statements from the developer. There are many many instances of the developers saying they've added things or fixed bugs, and none of it has actually happened. Controller support, certain bug fixes, changes to achievements, etc, were all clearly stated as done by the developer in communication with the player base. There is respect for actually responding to the community but blatant lies are uncalled for. Let's say we put all that aside and focus on the game. This isn't exactly much of a roguelike as you are able to get more predetermined upgrades and items in a run, and there is little variation in each match nor variations in your wands or chickens. For the asking price, Machick 2 is leaps and bounds beyond this original game. Some of the programming and design is fairly well done as a starter project but the developers actions have lead me to be far harsher on it. Furthermore, the game has a very bad habit of hijacking your sound device and influencing your whole devices sound. I have never witnessed that in a game before but it was starting to hurt my head, certain enemies would overload the sound engine and mess with my other audio such as Spotify/YouTube. The wand system is seriously tedious too, especially with how you are expected to progress and the "Craft 100 Wands" achievement that they said they reworked... [b]PROS[/b]: - Easy to understand - No need to think about your build [b]CONS[/b]: - Incredibly buggy - Terrible developer communication - No variation in runs - No metaprogression - Hijacking of sound device [i]Machick 2 is so much better, it is amazing what a single year difference could make.[/i]

I'm a sucker for "bullet-heaven" games and I definitely enjoyed Machick, but it's not in the top tier of the genre. The good: - As is usually the case, it is satisfying to grow stronger and stronger during a run, eventually becoming a force of destruction laying waste to all in my path. - There is a decent variety of weapons with different effects, and each has an upgraded form you can access by powering it up enough after level-ups. - Decent variety of enemies and environments, although the latter are not particularly inspired. - The gimmick of creating your own magic wand is really clever and engaging. As you play through runs you unlock new wand materials and elemental runes to imbue them with benefits. You also unlock pieces of pre-made wands with their own unique characteristics. This leads to fun customization possibilities, such as having your wand cause your enemies to drop money earlier on and focusing more on damage output later on. The bad: - The game crashed on me several times (although usually within the first minute or so of a run). - Some of the sound effects are blaringly obnoxious, particular when they layer on top of each other. I ended up lowering the volume of the sound effects to zero. - While the graphics are decent, they aren't very well thought-out. For instance, one of the abilities you can use is a team of tiny chicks that follow you around. They are so small it's easy to lose track of them altogether and it's hard to see what they contribute. Dropped gold looks similar to scattered flowers. Enemies drop gold in little bunches, even if the value of said gold is only 1. - There is an obnoxious achievement that involves creating 100 wands. Playing the game organically means you will eventually be able to construct extremely powerful wands that are pretty much as good as you can get. But if you want that achievement (and I did) then you'll have to spend time just creating and destroying wands in a loop, never using any of them. There are plenty of better "bullet heaven" games, but Machick is decent fun that kept me engaged for a while. Recommended for those who can't get enough of the genre.

This is a really competently made little game. If you’re looking for a bite-sized Survivors experience, I totally recommend this. I had fun with it, and finished everything in about 6 hours. You are a magic chicken (ma-chick) with a wand who need to defend their home from the frog scourge. The game brings two things to the table: first, the ability to modify your base attack by customizing your magic wand. This was a clever little system and I enjoyed toying around with it; while in some cases expensive parts = better, there was also room for playstyle customization (eg, I don’t think any of the elements were really inherently superior), and it was really satisfying to lose a run, make an upgrade to the run, and go back in and beat it. The focus on modifying your main attack for progress meant runs really felt in your hands; it also helped mitigate the small array of available weapons. Especially once you hit the 20 minute levels, you’re going to be grabbing every weapon — though personally I liked the trial-and-error of seeing which order I wanted to grab things in, what I wanted to pour levels into versus what can wait, etc. The wand was a neat little system and added a lot to the basic VS gameplay. The other thing it did I really liked was having level time scale with difficulty. So the first level is 10 minutes, then 15, 20, 30, and the last one is endless. Frankly I think more VS games should adopt this system (Army of Ruin also had it) — one of my few complaints about VS was that you could get very ‘stuck’ on levels, especially the first one, and having to live 30 minutes when you could barely get past 10 at the beginning could be pretty daunting. This way your beginning runs don’t feel so futile, and you get the satisfaction of beating a boss and clearing something much earlier, and the scale up is satisfying instead of every level being the same in terms of goal. Plus, frankly, as a person with a life, having to commit 30 minutes minimum to every run kind of sucks. My one complaint is the 100 wand achievement — I think I got like 15 naturally through clearing everything else, 50 is a stupid grind and 100 is bonkers, especially since the minigame can’t be automated easily. But on the whole this was a cute entry into the genre and I’m definitely going to grab the sequel.

[h1]Machick: 8.9h | 100% Achievements (24/24) Completed | Not Recommended[/h1] [i]I came expecting a magical world with magic chickens. I left with 83 crafted wands I've never used, a mute button, and a profound understanding of what "lukewarm" means.[/i] [h1]Achievement Breakdown[/h1] [b]Grindy Achievements:[/b] Yes (~3). [i][u]"Craft 20/50/100 Wands"[/u][/i] are the worst, you'll craft around 10-15 organically, then spam random wands to complete the rest. [b]Missable Achievements:[/b] No. [b]Difficult Achievements:[/b] No. The game is really easy; the 100% is just boring. [h1]What is Machick About?[/h1] [b]Machick[/b] is a [i]Vampire Survivors[/i]-style bullet heaven with a twist: instead of each character having a different weapon, you craft custom wands that change projectile types, damage stats, attack speed, and different buffs. You play as a magic chicken, survive timed waves, collect experience, and look at the screen questioning your life by the time you take into account it's your 6th play and you're doing the same thing over and over. [b]Pros:[/b] - The wand crafting [i]concept[/i] is genuinely neat - It's short enough that the 100% doesn't waste too much of your life [b]Cons:[/b] - Rerolls frequently give you the exact same thing you just discarded - Everything is janky: animations, UI, and enemies all feel unfinished - No kill tracker per weapon/passive - Zero build variety; every run plays identically with the same items and upgrades - Audio is broken: overlapping sound effects, broken volume sliders, and no meaningful music - Nothing is explained: chest upgrades, chicken stats, special wand scaling, you have to guess everything [u](More about the pros and cons in the in-depth review part below)[/u] [h1]Should You Buy This Game?[/h1] [b]No[/b]. Not even on a deep sale. [b]Machick[/b] isn't really bad, it's just meh. It has the ideas of a decent survivor clone but none of them actually work 100%. If you want a good survivor game with crafting, look elsewhere. The wand mechanic unfortunately doesn't carry this game alone. If you're here for easy achievements, then I guess you can buy it on sale since it doesn't really demand much of your brain. [h1]In-Depth Review[/h1] [h3]Visuals[/h3] [b]Machick[/b] blends pixel art with VFX effects, and it's.... alright. It's not ugly but I feel it doesn't have personality. It tries to give the enemies some fun designs but they are not really well portrayed. No chest opening animation, no proper enemy death animation, no level up animation. It's just bland. The weapon VFX are fine but nothing that will really catch your attention or make you feel powerful by looking at it. [h3]Soundtrack[/h3] This is genuinely one of the worst audio experiences I've had in a survivor game. The sound effects are low-quality, the music is forgettable, and the mixing is broken: even if you drag the SFX slider to minimum, the spells and explosions still overpower the music. Worse, sounds stack on top of each other with no limit, creating a cacophony of chirps and blasts that makes the game actively unpleasant to listen to. I muted the entire game after my third run and never turned it back on. [h3]The Game[/h3] [b]Machick[/b] follows the standard survivor formula: pick a level, survive for 10-15 minutes, kill the final boss, collect your rewards. There are 5 levels, with the last one stretching for as long as you can last. After each run, you spend gold on wand upgrades and unlock new chickens, although the latter doesn't really add or change anything to your gameplay. The wand crafting system should be the star. You pick a wand type that fires different projectiles, select different types of wood with different damage, attack speed, and buffs, slot in up to 5 elemental cores with different effects, and select different elemental runes to increase your power even further. Early on, it's really interesting to check all the different combinations. But here's the main problem: once you make one really strong wand, you never need to craft a new one again. The game doesn't incentivize variety. There are no enemy resistances, no level gimmicks that force you to adapt, no reason to ever touch the crafting bench after hour two. Which brings us to the [i][u]"Craft 20/50/100 Wands"[/u][/i] achievement. During a natural playthrough, you'll craft maybe 15 to 20 wands. To hit 100, you will see yourself making a bunch of random wands just to immediately dump them and keep the cycle going until the achievement pops. At least it doesn't take much; I believe it took me around 10-15 minutes. The reroll system is completely useless. You already start with 10 rerolls for the weapons/passives and 10 rerolls for special items, which are counted separately. The game's purpose is to turn off your brain and just pick all the weapons. Is there even a need for rerolls? The developers also believe there's no need for it because you can reroll items up to 5 times in a row and get the same options on all these 5 times. The UI is another low point. You can't quickly check your items and passives mid-run, you have to pause, navigate to another menu, go back manually (esc doesn't work for some reason) and then go back to your gameplay. This makes me wonder if they did any playtesting for this game or if the people that tested just didn't care enough to check... which is weird considering this is a survival game. There's no kill track per weapon so you can't actually see which one is stronger. Chest upgrades exist, but the game never explains what leveling them does or how long their respawn cooldown is. You're just leveling it up for the cheap dopamine. [h1]Completionist Tips[/h1] - Don't wait to craft 100 wands organically. Grind it as soon as you can by crafting the first wand, deleting it, and repeating. - Prioritize buying the upgrade that lets you increase the amount of cores in your wand. At the beginning you can use only 1 so try to get to 5 asap. Then buy all the cores as well, especially the double XP core. - Special wands are not worth using in my opinion. Get them just for the achievement. - Mute the game. Your ears will thank you. [h1]Conclusion[/h1] [b]Machick[/b] wants to be an easy, creative survival game, but while trying to be like that it loses the main core of a survival game which is thinking about your build and seeing how you're going to play each level to survive and get stronger. With mechanics not well explained, and characters and weapons feeling all the same. It just doesn't feel rewarding enough to keep going. Quite the opposite actually, if not for the achievements I would've dropped this way sooner. The genre lives and dies on "just one more run." [b]Machick[/b] kills that feeling after your first hour. I hope [b]Machick 2[/b] fixes what this game couldn't, because the idea deserves better.
